purpose: Complete source identity map for final.md; carried source IDs are preserved without rebinding. The complete received investigator and critic maps are retained below.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model (W3C Recommendation)
sources.released_version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation; current canonical TR URL; publication date shown on document; not a merge protocol
sources.locator: Abstract; sections 1.1–1.3, 3.1–3.2, 4.2 selectors; JSON-LD model
sources.observed_operation: Defines annotations as bodies related to one or more targets; target can be a SpecificResource with selectors/state; identifies annotation and target separately and supports portable JSON serialization.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The data model is transport-neutral and does not define synchronization or selector migration. Selector applicability depends on media type; consumers may ignore irrelevant selector types. External target metadata in an annotation is a hint, not authoritative target truth.
sources.applicability: Useful export/interchange structure for review thread body, target, selected region, and captured state; insufficient by itself for stable object identity or offline reconciliation.

sources.title: Loro v1.0.0 release notes
sources.released_version_or_commit: Loro 1.0.0 release page; stable encoding format announced for v1.0
sources.locator: Release overview and sections describing movable list/tree, history, stable encoding; release URL is named v1.0.0-beta
sources.observed_operation: Maintainer release material describes Loro as Rust/JS/Swift CRDT library, adds version control/history features, movable lists and trees, and states the 1.0 data format is stable.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A library merges operations; app intent and product-level comment semantics remain application responsibilities. Stable encoding is a format compatibility statement, not a policy guarantee for anchor behavior.
sources.applicability: A maintained alternative worth evaluating for movable hierarchical grouping and history, without selecting it for the proposed component.

sources.title: Loro JavaScript API Reference
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current API reference; page does not pin an immutable release; Loro 1.0 stable-format release is separately recorded in R02
sources.locator: LoroTree methods createNode/move/delete/getNodeByID/isNodeDeleted; TreeID and event types; API reference tree notes
sources.observed_operation: Provides stable TreeID-based create/move/delete access, a deleted-state query, movable list operations, and concurrent-move cycle prevention. API warns tree fractional indexing can interleave under concurrent insertions while preserving order.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The tree delete method removes a node and descendants. Fractional indexing is a distinct ordering policy; cycle prevention is automatic but does not resolve human meaning of a comment after replacement.
sources.applicability: Potential layout operation substrate; preserve a separate application object UUID and comment lineage, and test group/delete semantics against the selected version.

sources.title: Loro Tree tutorial
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current documentation; LoroTree API
sources.locator: Events section and node retrieval examples
sources.observed_operation: Tree diffs carry create/move/delete actions and old/new parent/index; event order follows causality; delete event represents target plus subtree and does not emit child-specific delete events.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A subtree delete is one event in this API; callers needing every anchored child to retain context must enumerate affected identities or keep independent comment anchors.
sources.applicability: Useful for grouping/ungrouping event interpretation, but group membership alone cannot determine whether a thread should move to a group or remain on its original child.

sources.title: Loro shallow snapshots
sources.released_version_or_commit: Loro 1.0 feature; current docs
sources.locator: Basic Usage, Content Redaction, Synchronization Limitations, Archive and Trim
sources.observed_operation: Shallow snapshot encodes current state while trimming operations before a chosen frontier; docs give a typical 70–90% size reduction and show removal of sensitive deleted text from the new snapshot.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Peers can sync only if they are based after the shallow snapshot point; all peers must receive the sanitized document for old content to be removed everywhere. Archiving full history preserves data that trimming was intended to remove.
sources.applicability: Demonstrates that history retention, storage growth, sync cutoffs, and privacy are coupled decisions; keep compact comment-context snapshots separately and disclose retention/archives.

sources.title: Y.Doc API
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current Yjs docs, API is on v13 line unless otherwise stated; stable v13.6.33 release record is R08
sources.locator: Y.Doc API; `doc.gc` property
sources.observed_operation: Exposes `doc.gc`; docs say setting it false disables garbage collection so old content can be restored. Transactions batch shared-type changes and emit updates after transaction.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page documents the control and effect but does not state a default value in the inspected text. Do not infer default from this page; verify exact pinned package before adopting.
sources.applicability: If comments or anchor evidence are stored inside a Y.Doc, garbage-collection settings directly affect whether deleted target context survives; keep required review history in a separately governed structure.

sources.title: Yjs internal model notes
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling `main` file; no immutable commit hash exposed in browser response. Yjs v13.6.33 release is separately recorded in R08.
sources.locator: Deletion section around lines 223–227; update/sync section around 242–249
sources.observed_operation: States that deletion does not retain when or which user deleted an item; when GC is enabled deleted content is discarded and a lightweight GC struct stores removed length; sync updates include delete sets and snapshots combine state vector plus delete set.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The no-author/no-time statement is about Yjs deletion metadata, not custom app fields. GC behavior is conditional on the document GC setting. The file is mutable main-branch documentation.
sources.applicability: Do not expect library tombstones alone to explain a review thread. Record app-level deletion actor/time/frontier/meaning only if policy and privacy permit, and keep comment records independent of GC-pruned content.

sources.title: Yjs issue #741: tombstone memory report
sources.source_type: Public upstream issue report; unresolved at access
sources.released_version_or_commit: Reporter says Yjs 13.6.27; issue opened 2025-10-21 and remains open in observed page
sources.locator: Issue description and environment
sources.observed_operation: Reporter supplies a reproducible repository and reports memory spikes for a long-lived document with roughly 10 million deleted structs; page describes document and encodeStateAsUpdate memory far above file size.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is a reporter claim/status, not a verified general benchmark or maintainer conclusion; behavior is tied to the reporter environment and v13.6.27.
sources.applicability: Treat retained deletion context as a measurable storage/memory risk and benchmark synthetic history volume; do not assume tombstones are free.

sources.title: Automerge conflict documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current docs; release month Aug 2026 reports Automerge 3.4.1, but this page does not pin a package build
sources.locator: What is a Conflict; `Automerge.getConflicts`; operation ID ordering
sources.observed_operation: Concurrent writes to the same property expose a deterministic winner and keep alternatives accessible through conflict inspection; a later assignment resolves the conflict. Winner ordering uses operation ID, not wall-clock time.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A deterministic winner is convergence behavior, not a judgment that a comment target or layout intent is semantically correct. Reading the ordinary property view can hide a concurrent alternative unless the app inspects conflicts.
sources.applicability: Preserve conflict alternatives and provenance for consequential anchor resolution; do not convert a mechanical winner into silent reattachment.

sources.title: Automerge merge rules
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current docs, not version-pinned
sources.locator: Map merge rules and list merge rules
sources.observed_operation: Documents concurrent map delete versus concurrent set as retaining the newly set value; list operations reference element IDs rather than raw numeric indices; concurrent insert/delete/update cases have explicit CRDT rules.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A concurrent set may make a map key visible again under the documented rule. It does not encode a product-level decision to undo a deliberate deletion or restore a user-visible object.
sources.applicability: Keep “layout replica convergence” separate from “review intent”; use application-level deletion/tombstone state and explicit undo/restore events.

sources.title: Automerge repository storage
sources.released_version_or_commit: Automerge Repo current docs; page not package-version pinned
sources.locator: Storage model; snapshots, incrementals, concurrent compaction
sources.observed_operation: Repo stores incremental changes and periodically compacts them into snapshots; concurrent compaction deletes only changes already incorporated, using document heads in snapshot identity.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is repo storage behavior, not Automerge core conflict semantics. Compaction preserves mergeable state/history according to the repo storage scheme; it is not user-visible comment retention policy.
sources.applicability: A useful storage option, but application-level tombstones, anchor context, and export retention still need a bounded policy.

sources.title: Automerge glossary: history compaction
sources.released_version_or_commit: Rolling current docs, not version-pinned
sources.locator: Compaction definition and tradeoffs
sources.observed_operation: Defines compaction as serializing current state without full history and notes it may be used for bandwidth/device constraints or to purge sensitive deleted content.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: After history compaction, the document may no longer sync with another replica that lacks a common ancestor. Purging one copy does not prove replicas/archives have also discarded content.
sources.applicability: Retention/privacy decisions must specify replica cutover, archive policy, and behavior for stale offline peers.

sources.title: Automerge project blog/current releases
sources.released_version_or_commit: Blog index accessed 2026-10-12; August 2026 entry names Automerge 3.4.1; Automerge Repo 2.0 release entry May 2025
sources.locator: Recent Posts: This Month in Automerge August 2026; Automerge 3.0 and Automerge Repo 2.0 entries
sources.observed_operation: Maintainer lists active Automerge releases and Repo 2.0 as current ecosystem context; Automerge 3.0 release describes >10x memory reduction while retaining history and backward-compatible file format with v2.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Blog release statements are maintainer claims and do not replace testing the pinned dependency. Repo handles networking/storage; Automerge core is network-agnostic.
sources.applicability: Evidence that maintained collaboration mechanisms include a core CRDT plus optional repository layer; compare both layers and their operational responsibilities.

sources.title: Excalidraw reconcileElements implementation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mutable `master` at access; no immutable commit hash exposed in browser response; public issue R17 says 0.18.1 for separate reported case
sources.locator: `shouldDiscardRemoteElement`, lines 456–497; `reconcileElements`, lines 547–619
sources.observed_operation: Reconciliation matches by element ID, discards a remote copy when the local item is being edited or has a greater version, and breaks equal-version ties with the lower versionNonce; it appends unmatched local elements, then orders/heals indices.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This is one library’s record-version protocol, not a general merge law. An absent remote record does not by itself remove the local record in this function; deletion needs an explicit record/version state in the caller’s data.
sources.applicability: Concrete whiteboard caller/test surface to study; use as comparative behavior and regression-test inspiration, not as the proposal’s selected merge engine.

sources.title: Excalidraw collaboration caller
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mutable `master` at access; current caller source, no commit SHA exposed in browser response
sources.locator: `_reconcileElements` around lines 3480–3505 and `handleRemoteSceneUpdate` around lines 3555–3567
sources.observed_operation: Caller gets scene elements including deleted entries, restores remote elements with prior local context, invokes reconcileElements, bumps versions, then applies remote update with captureUpdate NEVER. It uses the same routine for room sync and persisted scene results.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: This integration relies on the library’s ID/version/deleted record conventions and repair/bump behavior; it does not model comment intent or external export.
sources.applicability: Shows deletion/tombstone state and caller post-processing are part of reconciliation, so a component must define its persistence and caller contract.

sources.title: Excalidraw issue #3795: import resets ID/version
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2021-07-04; closed with linked PR #3797 (issue page exposes link; patch retrieval unavailable)
sources.locator: Issue description and numbered reproduction steps
sources.observed_operation: Reported import reused the same element ID and an older version after a delete, causing later save/sync comparison to treat the imported replacement as a no-op; issue proposes new IDs or version bump/nonce regeneration.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue is closed and linked to #3797; its issue body documents the failure mode, not the exact merged fix or all current-version behavior.
sources.applicability: Strong regression-test precedent: imported/recreated data must not make an old object appear current or silently defeat a delete; identical appearance does not establish identity.

sources.title: Excalidraw issue #11933: remote index healing/version report
sources.source_type: Open public issue report; not maintainer-confirmed at access
sources.released_version_or_commit: Opened 2026-08-22; reporter claims repro on @excalidraw/excalidraw 0.18.1 and current master; still Open, no linked PR in observed metadata
sources.locator: Summary, deterministic repro, root cause, status metadata
sources.observed_operation: Reporter supplies a runnable single-client reproduction where repeated remote index repair allegedly increments record version, after which reconcileElements discards a genuine newer peer edit.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Unresolved reporter claim; neither reproducer nor reported production path was executed in this research. The inspected current source does contain a version-based discard rule and post-merge index healing.
sources.applicability: Treat as an integration hazard to test at the remote repair boundary, not a verified defect or a reason to reject the upstream library.

sources.title: Excalidraw reconcileElements test suite
sources.released_version_or_commit: Mutable master; immutable commit not identified in inspected page
sources.locator: elements reconciliation suite; version selection cases, concurrent convergence, unique-index assertion, re-reconciliation, identical elements
sources.observed_operation: Tests version-based selection, stable unique indices, convergence across input order, and repeated reconciliation. The inspected suite does not model comment anchors or thread intent.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: These are Excalidraw implementation tests; they do not validate this proposed component or prove complete deletion behavior.
sources.applicability: Direct evidence for C1 and a baseline for comparing technical merge invariants with missing comment semantics.

sources.title: Loro issue 938: redo with recreated TreeID
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue page; no package version or immutable commit identified in inspected page
sources.locator: Issue title and redo reproduction
sources.observed_operation: The issue describes redo recreating a LoroTree node with a new TreeID and losing associated text across separate undo steps.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Issue report was not executed or treated as maintainer-confirmed behavior.
sources.applicability: Supplemental caution that engine node identity and application object/comment identity need explicit restore semantics; it does not contradict the proposed independent application IDs.

reviser_rechecks.title: Excalidraw reconcileElements test suite
reviser_rechecks.released_version_or_commit: Mutable master observed 2026-10-12; no immutable commit SHA captured in the inspected page.
reviser_rechecks.locator: Test helper and reconcileElements cases, especially lines 1075-1195, 1227-1492, and 1496-1633 in the rendered page.
reviser_rechecks.observed_operation: Direct inspection confirmed cases for expected local/remote record selection; unique output indices; same resulting IDs when swapping local and remote input roles; repeated reconciliation; concurrent element-array cases; and identical ID/version/versionNonce/index records.
reviser_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: Inspection only; no test command was run. The suite tests Excalidraw record reconciliation and does not model comment IDs, anchor selectors, thread visibility after delete, or semantic reassignment. Mutable branch means this is point-in-time evidence.
reviser_rechecks.applicability: Repairs the repository-tests discovery gap in C1 while bounding what upstream tests establish; it does not validate the proposed component.

reviser_rechecks.title: Excalidraw reconcileElements implementation
reviser_rechecks.released_version_or_commit: Mutable master observed 2026-10-12; no immutable commit SHA captured in the inspected page.
reviser_rechecks.locator: shouldDiscardRemoteElement and reconcileElements, rendered page lines 456-618.
reviser_rechecks.observed_operation: Direct inspection confirmed the local edit/newer-version/lower-versionNonce selection rule, unmatched local record retention, fractional-index ordering, and invalid-index repair.
reviser_rechecks.governing_condition_default_exception: Implementation-specific behavior only. It does not define application comment intent, and the mutable URL is not a reproducible pinned revision.
reviser_rechecks.applicability: Cross-checks the implementation claims used to frame C01 and the bounded record-reconciliation alternative.

critic_disposition.C1: accept_and_amend: direct C01 inspection confirms useful reconciler tests but no comment-anchor/thread intent coverage.
critic_disposition.C2: retain_uncertainty: owner decisions remain open and explicitly listed in final.md.
critic_disposition.C3: accept: mutable master URLs and lack of inspected immutable SHA remain explicit limitations.
